messages:
sam.sales: Heads up — ACME POC stuck on SSO + SCIM during onboarding. Okta shows SCIM 409 on group create and SAML login works, but Dedicated pool API key calls return 401 when using SAML assertion. Anyone seen this?

anya-se: Ugh. Quick checklist: 1) SCIM service app token in Okta 2) group attribute mappings (name vs displayName) 3) user provisioning enabled. Can you paste the SCIM error body?

sam.sales: Here's the SCIM response from Okta: 
```
{"status":409,"detail":"Group displayName already exists","error":"conflict"}
```
Also they used attribute "name":"Engineering" vs our expected "displayName" — suspect mapping mismatch.

ravi-se: That explains 409. Our SCIM handles displayName as unique key for groups. Okta sometimes sends `name` by default. Fix: in Okta SCIM app -> Attribute Mappings -> map group.displayName <- group.name. Also re-sync after changing.

sam.sales: After mapping change they still can't provision users into Dedicated pool role — tokens from our Hosted API work, but when we try to mint a Dedicated service token via SAML assertion it fails with 401. Error: "invalid_audience" from token endpoint.

ravi-se: For Dedicated the token audience must be `redwood-dedicated-<pool-id>`. Confirm the audience value in their SAML assertion and check our docs: https://redwood.example/docs/dedicated/saml-audience. If they're using generic audience it'll be rejected.

anya-se: Also remind them to add our Dedicated OIDC client as an IDP-initiated app in Okta and to set the ACS URL to the dedicated callback. I've sent step-by-step to their admin.

infra-bot: deploy-log: created temporary support key redwood-support-177250 for testing (expires in 24h).

sam.sales: OK trying the fix now. If this doesn't work we'll ask for screenshots of the SAML assertion and the Okta SCIM mappings. Thanks :thumbsup:
